name: How much contingency should I budget for a bathroom remodel in an older home?

mainEntity.name: How much contingency should I budget for a bathroom remodel in an older Los Angeles home?
mainEntity.text: How much contingency should I budget for a bathroom remodel in an older Los Angeles home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes are more likely to reveal surprises once the bathroom is opened up, so a contingency reserve is essential. The right amount depends on age, condition, and how much of the room is being changed, but the key idea is to keep a separate budget for hidden repairs rather than spending every dollar on finishes. Common surprises include damaged subfloors, outdated wiring, corroded plumbing, framing issues, and failed waterproofing. In Los Angeles neighborhoods with older housing stock, these issues are especially common during full gut remodels. Homeowners should ask the contractor what kinds of hidden conditions they have seen in similar homes and whether the estimate includes an explicit allowance or contingency line. It is better to plan for the possibility of extra work than to value-engineer the design after demolition starts. A well-planned contingency helps keep the project moving without sacrificing safety or finish quality.
acceptedAnswer.description: For older homes, a contingency is important because hidden plumbing, water damage, and electrical issues are common. A practical contingency is typically a separate reserve beyond the base bid so surprise repairs do not force a design compromise or project stop.
